newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 19.

text.p: Nats in damage control: National Party Cabinet ministers were in damage control at the weekend as they tried to pacify angry and worried delegates at two party conferences. Page 2.
Coalition ready to crumble -- Prebble: The Coalition Government's days were numbered, ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble said on Sunday. Page 2.
Thumbs-down for super scheme: Compulsory superannuation is dead in the water if the attitude of delegates at a National Party conference on Sunday is anything to go by. Page 2.
Bolger seeks new ways to fight crime: Prime Minister Jim Bolger is looking for new ways to fight crime, and initiatives could be disclosed in next month's Budget. Page 2.

L-Day for Colonial on Aussie, NZ markets: Colonial Group will list on the New Zealand and Australian Stock Exchange today and has set a final institutional price for each stapled share and option at A$3.50. Page 14.
Spending by local bodies 'inflationary': The Manufacturers Federation criticised spending by local authorities, saying it was inflationary. Page 15.
Police disarm rival Asian groups: Escalating tension between rival groups of Asian youths in Christchurch resulted in a small arsenal of assorted weapons being seized by police on Sunday.

Stowaway to marry sailor, says magazine: A stowaway who hid on board a ship for three months with her twin sister will marry one of the Malaysian sailors who looked after her, a women's magazine has reported.
Birch, Creech shun super plan: Two more cabinet heavy- weights have come out against compulsory superannuation, meaning at least six of National's top ten line-up are now opposed.

More privatisation, but which assets?: The sell-off of more state corporations has been mooted by the Minister for State Owned Enterprises, but Jenny Shipley is not saying which companies are possible candidates for privatisation.

Uncertain ironsand message from BHP: BHP New Zealand Steel officials brought an uncertain message at the weekend to Taharoa, an isolated settlement on Waikato's west coast and site of an ironsand mining operation.

Golden growth in Asia loses sheen: The golden Asian growth story is becoming tarnished because of a change in economic circumstances which will affect countries with a dependence on exports most, Morgan Stanley says in a research paper.

CNG sales decline continues: Fall off in popularity flies in face of world trend: Latest figures from Enerco, one of the main retailers of CNG, show a continuation of the steady decline in the use of the gas.

Toyota enters used-import car market: Toyota New Zealand is making a full scale entry into the used-car market using its former commercial vehicle assembly plant in Christchurch to refurbish local and imported used vehicles.
